title: The hypertrophy series: defining hard sets
summary: NH defines hard sets as repeatable sets in a relevant intensity window ended by muscular failure, and argues they produce the highest-quality tonnage. Unlike lifters who only do hard sets in their strength work, he makes every post-warm-up set a hard set and stops once they turn artificial.
claims: Hard sets are the most important sets in a program because they produce the highest-quality tonnage
Make as high a percentage of your total tonnage as possible come from hard sets
A hard set takes place in a selective, challenging intensity window, is pushed to failure, and can be repeated enough to accumulate tonnage
A set that buries you so much you can only do it once every 15 days is not a hard set, because it cannot be repeated continuously in the program
Every session should contain some hard sets, but not too many; past a certain point they stop being hard sets
A 100-rep set failed at rep 88 is not a hard set: the intensity window is irrelevant and failure is likely cardiovascular (an artificial rather than organic hard set)
A hard set is always ended by muscular failure: the muscle's endurance could not take the load and you had to stop
Beginners can do fewer hard sets because they lack muscular endurance and work capacity; the more advanced you get, the more hard sets you can handle
How many hard sets you need varies by body part and by experience with each movement pattern; some muscle groups need several hard sets because they can handle them

Many lifters build to hard sets only in their strength work, then do volume and accessories with no hard sets, so most of their quality tonnage comes from strength work; bodybuilders should do the opposite
If hard sets in the opening strength work kill your ability to do hard sets for the rest of the session, they are not worth it, because the following movements make up most of the tonnage
Every set he does after warm-ups is a hard set pushed to failure, recovering close to baseline but never 100%, and he quits before sets become artificial
Stop doing hard sets on a lift once you can no longer hit your reps with the weight (e.g. close-grip bench at 200 lb) or would have to strip the bar; beyond that sets are submaximal
He does 3-4 sets on most lifts because that is where hard sets shine, letting every movement pattern in the session get only hard sets
A body part split suits hard sets even better because each body part gets its own high-quality tonnage
exercises: stop sets once the target weight can no longer be repeated for reps
